intro_en: IMO-Bench is a three-capability evaluation suite built by mathematics Olympiad medalists and mathematicians. The paper snapshot contains the 400-item IMO-AnswerBench, 60-item IMO-ProofBench, and 1,000-item IMO-GradingBench, separately evaluating short-answer correctness, proof quality, and the ability to grade proofs. Each branch uses a different evaluation context and metric.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2511.01846 and the official google-deepmind/superhuman imobench release. The paper snapshot defines three complementary benchmarks rather than a sequential pipeline. IMO-AnswerBench contains 400 robustified, verifiable short-answer problems, balanced across four IMO categories, and uses a Gemini 2.5 Pro AnswerAutoGrader for semantic equivalence. IMO-ProofBench contains 60 proof problems, split into 30 Basic and 30 Advanced; the Advanced set comprises 18 novel medalist-authored problems, 6 robustified IMO 2024 problems, and 6 USAMO 2025 problems. Human experts receive the problem, candidate solution, reference solution, and specific grading guidelines and assign integer 0–7 grades; proof results are percentages of maximum points with basic, advanced, and source slices. The validated ProofAutoGrader is shown only as a scalable proxy, not a replacement for primary human grades. IMO-GradingBench contains 1,000 advanced-proof model solutions with expert 0–7 scores balanced into labels 7/6/1/0; models see only the problem and proposed solution, and are measured by four-way accuracy and mean absolute error. The current official project later adds a 60-item IMO-LeanProofBench, which is intentionally excluded from this paper-snapshot diagram.
